Speaker: Street Weirdo
Text: Pullman by night? In THIS old heap? That mountain eats such rides for cheap.

Speaker: Street Weirdo
Text: I-90 lifts from Seattle's sea-level shore to three thousand feet where the Pass-winds roar.

Speaker: Street Weirdo
Text: Ask about the pass
Result/Response: Past North Bend it's chains or a prayer — pick one, pal, and climb up there.

Speaker: Street Weirdo
Text: Give him a buck
Result/Response: A giver! How noble, how dumb — you'll die as humble as you've become.

Speaker: Street Weirdo
Text: Just drive

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: The pass turns cruel, the snow won't quit — chains beat a physics class dug in a pit.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Snoqualmie's mood can turn and bite 'twixt North Bend's calm and the summit's white.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Buy chains
Effect: Snow-chains buff + reveals snow hazard; ends

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Eighty bucks? Let's talk.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: How bad is it up there, really?

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Thanks anyway — I'll risk it

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Fifty-five cash — no receipt, no refund, no eye; that's my whole pitch, so buy or say bye.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Deal
Result/Response: He sold you chains that just look tough. Society rolls on, unbothered enough. (35% case)

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Back to full price

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Walk away

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Bad enough I'm here and not in bed — whiteout up top, and the plows are losing, it's said.

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Fine. The chains.
Effect: Returns to node: greet; reveals snow hazard

Speaker: Chain Guy
Text: Thank him and leave

Speaker: Ski Bum
Text: Past the tunnel it's whiteout, thick and dread — slow is smooth, and smooth is not-yet-dead.

Speaker: Ski Bum
Text: Snoqualmie's summit, three-oh-one-five high, is the lowest I-90 Cascade pass you'll spy.

Speaker: Ski Bum
Text: Buy his thermos
Result/Response: Coffee so strong it could strip a door — you're wide awake and craving more.

Speaker: Ski Bum
Text: Ask the safe line

Speaker: Ski Bum
Text: Wave and go

Speaker: Long-Haul Mike
Text: The Vantage wind flings semis like carts astray — two hands on the wheel, or you'll blow away.

Speaker: Long-Haul Mike
Text: At Vantage the Columbia's crossing runs wide, with bare, hard crosswinds on every side.

Speaker: Long-Haul Mike
Text: Take the wind tip
Result/Response: Lean in, don't fight it — that's the trick; out here you bend, or the wind hits quick.

Speaker: Long-Haul Mike
Text: Split his fuel run
Result/Response: Half the diesel he swore he'd hand — that's trucker math, you understand. (30% case)

Speaker: Long-Haul Mike
Text: Head out

Speaker: Farm Worker
Text: Real station's far — a hike, a slog; I've a jerry can out back… don't mind the color or the smog.

Speaker: Farm Worker
Text: Round Othello the Basin's irrigated and wide — long dark stretches, no service, no guide.

Speaker: Farm Worker
Text: Buy the can
Result/Response: That was NOT just gas, it's plain — the engine coughs and bucks in pain. (20% case)

Speaker: Farm Worker
Text: Ask about the road ahead
Result/Response: Watch for tractors dark as pitch — they own these nights, and every ditch.

Speaker: Farm Worker
Text: Risk it on empty

Speaker: Startup Founder
Text: Our app dodges every trap clear to Pullman's gate — freemium, of course; the free tier's the letdown you'll hate.

Speaker: Startup Founder
Text: Bellevue rose from a sleepy suburb's hush to glass-tower tech in two decades' rush.

Speaker: Startup Founder
Text: Buy premium
Result/Response: It actually works — two traps glide by unseen; she's already pitching a Series B, it seems. (success) / 'Servers are scaling!' she chirps — then the app falls flat; and so does your sixty, just like that. (fail)

Speaker: Startup Founder
Text: Ask for the free version

Speaker: Startup Founder
Text: Keep your data

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: I need a pass-bound lift, that's true — cash up front, no chit-chat too; best offer you'll hear the whole day through.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Issaquah rests where the Cascades rear up, the last place the suburbs finally give up.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Pick her up
Result/Response: She pays, reads the curves better than your GPS could, then's gone at the summit — a passenger good. (success) / Turns out she's on some watch-list, it seems — now you're right beside it, in the cops' bad dreams. (fail)

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Take gas money, no ride
Result/Response: 'Cold. Respect,' she says, unfazed — hands you a twenty and walks off unamazed.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Drive on

Speaker: Park Ranger
Text: Elk cross at dusk and don't check their blind side — and neither, it seems, do you when you ride.

Speaker: Park Ranger
Text: The wooded Cle Elum run, foothill-lined, is prime elk country of the roaming kind.

Speaker: Park Ranger
Text: Heed the warning
Result/Response: Slow at the tree lines, mind your speed — they're bigger than your car's whole creed.

Speaker: Park Ranger
Text: Point her at a 'lost hiker' up the road
Result/Response: She radios it in, thrown off the scent — your record breathes; the heat's misspent.

Speaker: Park Ranger
Text: Nod and leave

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Rodeo's in, so the coffee's fresh and the regulars are wild; you look on the run from something, child — pie?

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Coffee & pie
Result/Response: Best call you've made the whole trip long — low bar, sure, but it's not wrong.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: What's ahead of me?

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Just the check, thanks

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Well, look who survived the road's mean tricks — same booth's free, and you're getting pie; don't fight it, that's the fix.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: The usual
Result/Response: 'Knew it,' she grins; the pie appears before you've sat, allaying fears.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Any news up the road?

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Just passing through — take care

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Past Vantage the wind will part your hair through the screen — all morning the truckers came in white and green.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Ellensburg's a rodeo-college town, Kittitas' pride, roughly the halfway point of your statewide ride.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Better fuel up on pie then
Result/Response: Smart — nobody fights the wind and wins when their stomach's thin.

Speaker: Diner Waitress
Text: Thank her and hit the road

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Few stop in Hatton, dear, it's true — I keep gas for the ones who do, and cookies… but the gas is safer for you.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Hatton's a speck on WA-26's thread, 'twixt Othello and Washtucna, sparse and spread.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Buy her gas
Result/Response: Drive safe, or don't, my dear — either way, the news'll reach my ear.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Safer? What's in the cookies?

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Why Hatton, of all places?

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Politely flee

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Butter and sugar and a recipe old — one the county begged me to leave untold; one won't hurt you… or so I'm told.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Take a cookie
Result/Response: Strangely restoring, warm to the bone — you feel watched, but not alone. (70%) / You blink, and twenty minutes have flown — that's one fine cookie you've been thrown. (30%)

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Maybe the gas instead

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Decline politely and leave

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Somebody must watch this stretch, my dear; the road claims the careless who wander near — I just tidy the mess they leave here.

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: …About that gas

Speaker: Roadside Grandma
Text: Thank her and back away slowly

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: Three wrecks a week I haul from this bend — business is good, which should worry you, friend.

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: Washtucna's a thin wheat-country line, with long, long gaps 'twixt help and sign.

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: Prepay a tow discount
Result/Response: Crash, and I'll judge you — but only a bit; call it a discount on your fit.

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: Have her bang out a dent
Result/Response: A mallet, a grunt, a whack, a tad — and your car looks marginally less sad.

Speaker: Tow Driver
Text: Wave her off

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: Basin-bound? Top your coolant off right here — past Vantage the shade quits and the gauge climbs, I fear.

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: East of the Cascades the road drops to high desert's face — long, hot, and shadeless, the Columbia Basin's embrace.

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: Top off the coolant
Result/Response: He fills the radiator, spins the fan with care: 'That'll hold — probably. Say a prayer.'

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: Fill your jug from his hose
Result/Response: Warm hose water — not cold, but wet; he waves off your coins, no debt.

Speaker: Shade-Tree Mechanic
Text: I'll risk it

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: Ice-cold lemonade, mister — best in the Basin, we swear! (It's also the ONLY one anywhere.)

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: The Columbia Basin bakes and reels each summer's turn — past the Saddle Mountains, triple digits burn.

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: Buy the whole pitcher
Result/Response: Worth every cent you're giving — your parched tongue rejoins the living.

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: Just one cup
Result/Response: Cold and impossibly sweet, that sip — you smack your lips and resume the trip.

Speaker: Lemonade Kids
Text: Wave and go

Speaker: Nervous Student
Text: I missed the last bus and my finals won't wait — I can pay; just drive like my mom's at the gate.

Speaker: Nervous Student
Text: Seatbelt. Both hands. Great. Perfect. Love it.

Speaker: Nervous Student
Text: You're doing great. I'm saying that for both of us.

Speaker: Nervous Student
Text: We lived! Here — take it before I count it.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Need a lift up the road a spell — I chip in for gas, don't scream, ride well, and tip good coin for a story you tell.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Music's yours, pedal's yours. Impress me.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Is that all this thing does? Kidding. Mostly.

Speaker: Hitchhiker
Text: Decent run. Here's the fare.

Speaker: Desert Oddball
Text: I need to be gone from here, and swift — and skip any cops, if you catch my drift.

Speaker: Desert Oddball
Text: If anyone asks, I've been asleep since Tuesday.

Speaker: Desert Oddball
Text: He checks the mirror more than you do.

Speaker: Desert Oddball
Text: You never saw me. The money saw you, though.

Speaker: Old-Timer

Speaker: Old-Timer

Speaker: Old-Timer
